text:
Episode 1: Dragonstone
The story opens in the Riverlands at the Twins. Walder Frey hosts a feast for every Frey who helped in the Red Wedding. He calls them together under the pretense of sharing plans. Servants pour wine from the Arbor. Walder insults his new wife Kitty Frey, saying he will not waste good wine on a woman. He toasts his family for slaughtering the Starks: King Robb, his pregnant wife Talisa, their unborn child, and Lady Catelyn. The Freys laugh nervously.

Then the Freys start choking and dying from the poisoned wine. The man who looks like Walder scolds them for leaving one wolf alive, saying the sheep are never safe. He pulls off his face to reveal Arya Stark. She has used a stolen face to disguise herself as Walder and kill the men responsible for her family's massacre. She spares Kitty Frey and the servants. Arya tells them the North remembers and that winter came for House Frey. She walks away from the piles of dead Freys.

Later, Arya rides south on a horse she acquired. She meets a group of young Lannister soldiers camping. They sing a song about hands of gold and a woman's warm hands. They offer her rabbit meat and blackberry wine. The soldiers are homesick and talk about missing their families. They ask why she rides south. Arya says she is going to King's Landing to kill the queen. The soldiers laugh, thinking it a joke. Arya smiles and laughs with them.

Elsewhere in the snowy Riverlands, Sandor Clegane travels north with the Brotherhood Without Banners: Beric Dondarrion, Thoros of Myr, and others. They stop at an abandoned farmhouse. Sandor recognizes it and says it is unsafe, but Beric insists they stay. Inside they find the frozen corpses of a farmer and his young daughter Sally. Years earlier Sandor and Arya had met these two. The father had killed his daughter and then himself to spare them from starving.

Sandor talks with Beric about why the Lord of Light keeps bringing Beric back. Beric does not know. Sandor says he does not believe in divine justice after seeing the farmer and girl die that way. Thoros urges Sandor to look into the fire. At first Sandor sees only logs. Then he sees a vision: the Wall of ice, a castle where the Wall meets the sea (Eastwatch-by-the-Sea), a mountain shaped like an arrowhead, and thousands of the dead marching. Beric asks if Sandor now believes they have a purpose.

Later Thoros finds Sandor outside burying the farmer and Sally in the snow. They bury the bodies together. Sandor tries to say words for the Seven but cannot remember them. He simply says the dead deserved better.

At Winterfell, King in the North Jon Snow holds a meeting with the Northern lords and ladies. He organizes defenses against the Night King and the army of the dead. He orders all maesters to search for dragonglass because it kills White Walkers and is now more valuable than gold. He sends Tormund Giantsbane and the wildlings to man Eastwatch-by-the-Sea, since they have already seen the dead at Hardhome. Jon decrees that every able-bodied person from age 10 to 60 must train for combat, including women and girls. Lord Robett Glover objects to arming his young granddaughter. Young Lady Lyanna Mormont of Bear Island speaks up fiercely. She says she will not sit idle and that every girl on Bear Island will train. The lords fall silent and agree.

Jon turns to the castles of Last Hearth (Umber) and Karhold (Karstark). These houses fought with the Boltons against the Starks. Lord Yohn Royce wants the castles destroyed. Sansa Stark argues they should strip the houses of their lands as punishment. Jon refuses. He will not punish children for their fathers' crimes. He calls forward young Ned Umber and Alys Karstark. They are terrified children. Jon asks them to reaffirm loyalty to House Stark. They kneel. Jon says the mistakes of the past no longer matter. Littlefinger watches and smiles.

In private Jon scolds Sansa for questioning him in front of the lords. It undermines him. Sansa says their father and brother Robb were too trusting and died for it. She wants Jon to be smarter. A message arrives from Queen Cersei Lannister. She claims she does not oppose the Starks reclaiming the North from the Boltons but demands they bend the knee to her. Jon focuses on the dead. Sansa warns him not to underestimate Cersei.

Brienne of Tarth spars with Podrick Payne in the yard. Podrick struggles. Tormund watches and comments. Littlefinger tries to needle Sansa about looking unhappy. Sansa says she wants peace. Brienne sees the exchange and walks over. Littlefinger leaves quickly. Brienne asks why Littlefinger is still there. Sansa says the Knights of the Vale helped win the Battle of the Bastards. She knows what Littlefinger wants.

Beyond the Wall, a column of White Walkers on undead horses leads a vast army of wights through a snowstorm. The horde includes undead giants. Bran Stark and Meera Reed reach the gate under Castle Black. Acting Lord Commander Eddison Tollett and Night's Watch brothers challenge them. Meera introduces herself and Bran. Bran proves he knows Edd by mentioning the Fist of the First Men and Hardhome and that Edd has seen the dead. Edd lets them inside, looking nervously at the lands beyond the Wall.

In King's Landing, Queen Cersei shows Jaime a huge map of Westeros painted on the floor. Jaime is silent and angry because of their son Tommen's death after Cersei blew up the Great Sept. Cersei tells him Tyrion has returned with Daenerys Targaryen and her armada. Jaime predicts Daenerys will land at Dragonstone, her birthplace, which is empty after Stannis left and has deep water for ships. Cersei lists enemies: Dorne in the south, the Tyrells in the west/reach, the Starks in the north.

Jaime says they are losing. All their children are dead. Kevan and Lancel died in the Sept explosion. There is no Lannister line left for the Iron Throne. Cersei says Tommen betrayed them. She and Jaime are the only Lannisters who matter. Jaime says they need allies. He reports House Frey has been wiped out. Cersei reminds him she has listened to their father Tywin for forty years and learned.

(The episode continues with more setup of alliances, Daenerys's arrival at Dragonstone with her fleet, Unsullied, Dothraki, and dragons. She walks the empty halls of her ancestral home, touches the Painted Table, and claims it as her seat. The full narrative builds the sense of converging threats: the dead in the North, Cersei consolidating power, Daenerys returning home ready for war, Arya hunting, the Brotherhood seeing visions, and Jon preparing the North while tensions rise with Sansa and Littlefinger. Every thread emphasizes winter is here and the game of thrones continues amid greater dangers.)

(Expanded details from the wiki cover the full feast revenge, Sandor's vision and burial, the full Winterfell council with forgiveness of the children lords, the private Jon-Sansa talk, Brienne-Pod-Tormund-Littlefinger moments, Bran and Meera's arrival, and the Cersei-Jaime map and family discussion. The story closes with Daenerys landing and entering Dragonstone, dragons flying overhead, setting her claim.)
1
)

Episode 2: Stormborn
A thunderstorm rages over Dragonstone. Tyrion, Varys, and Daenerys talk about the stormy night of her birth. Varys says Cersei's hold on Westeros is weak. Tyrion advises Daenerys not to burn the Seven Kingdoms. She should forge alliances instead. Daenerys questions Varys about serving her father the Mad King and then Robert Baratheon. Varys explains Robert was better than Aerys at first but had little interest in ruling.

Daenerys confronts Varys about the assassins sent after her as a child. Varys says he had no choice: pretend loyalty to Robert or lose his head. She distrusts his shifting sides. Varys stands firm. He says bad rulers do not deserve blind loyalty. He tells his story as a castrated slave boy. His loyalty is to the people. If she wants only blind loyalty she can kill him, but he is more useful alive. He believes she is the people's last hope. Daenerys accepts his service if he will tell her honestly when she is wrong. She warns that if he betrays her she will burn him. Varys says he expects nothing less from the Mother of Dragons.

Melisandre the red priestess arrives. She thinks Daenerys might be the Prince That Was Promised. Varys asks about her service to Stannis. Missandei notes that the High Valyrian word for prince is gender-neutral. Melisandre says it could be Daenerys or Jon Snow, who has united the North and wildlings against the dead. Tyrion vouches for Jon. Daenerys tells Tyrion to invite Jon to Dragonstone—and Jon must bend the knee.

In the Chamber of the Painted Table, Yara Greyjoy and Ellaria Sand push for an immediate attack on King's Landing. Tyrion argues against killing tens of thousands of innocents. Ellaria mocks him. Tyrion reminds her she poisoned his niece Myrcella for revenge. Ellaria does not deny it and regrets Oberyn died helping free Tyrion. Daenerys orders Ellaria to respect her Hand.

Tyrion proposes a plan: Tyrell and Dornish forces siege King's Landing. Unsullied under Grey Worm take Casterly Rock to cut off Cersei's retreat and hit Lannister morale. The Greyjoy fleet escorts Ellaria to Sunspear to gather Dornish forces, then ferries them to King's Landing. This avoids the Stormlands and starts the siege sooner. Daenerys agrees. She will not be Queen of the Ashes. Everyone consents.

Daenerys keeps Olenna Tyrell behind. She knows Olenna wants revenge on Cersei, not love for Daenerys. Daenerys wants peace. Olenna says there was never lasting peace under the Mad King or other Targaryens. Tyrion is clever but Olenna outlasted clever men by ignoring them. The lords are sheep. Daenerys is a dragon. Be a dragon.

Missandei visits Grey Worm before he sails for Casterly Rock. Grey Worm says she is his weakness. The Good Masters of Astapor trained Unsullied by facing their worst fears: dogs, heights, drowning. Only the fit survived. He was the most fearless until her. Missandei says she has fears too. She kisses him, undresses, and they share an intimate night. Grey Worm is hesitant about his scars but yields.

In King's Landing, Cersei speaks to Reach nobles including Randyll Tarly. She urges them not to follow the Tyrells to Daenerys. She warns of Dothraki and Unsullied pillaging and raping. Randyll notes Daenerys has three dragons. Qyburn says he is working on a solution.

Jaime meets Randyll privately. He wants Randyll as his general. Randyll is loyal to Olenna and wary of Lannisters who kill at weddings. Jaime reminds him of his oath to the Iron Throne. Cersei is better than a foreign queen with foreign armies. Cersei will make Randyll Warden of the South.

Qyburn takes Cersei to the dragon skulls under the Red Keep. Spies report one of Daenerys's dragons was wounded by a spear in Meereen, so they are not invincible. He shows a scorpion ballista. Cersei tests it on Balerion the Black Dread's massive skull. The bolt pierces it. She is pleased.

At Winterfell, Jon, Sansa, and Davos discuss Tyrion's letter inviting Jon to Dragonstone. Sansa remembers Tyrion was kind but worries it is a trap. Jon confirms it is real because of a private line Tyrion once said to him about dwarfs and bastards. Davos says Daenerys would be a strong ally against the dead because of fire. Jon decides not to go yet.

Days later a message arrives from Sam at the Citadel. There is a huge vein of dragonglass under Dragonstone. Jon calls the lords. He will go to Dragonstone to get the dragonglass and convince Daenerys to fight the dead. Lords Royce and Glover distrust Targaryens because of the Mad King. Lyanna Mormont wants Jon to stay. Jon says the fight against the dead is more important. The North is his home and he will always fight for it. He names Sansa regent in his absence. She accepts.

(The full story continues with more Northern politics, Littlefinger's manipulations, Sam's discoveries at the Citadel about dragonglass and ancient threats, Theon and Yara sailing, and Euron's attack on their fleet. Yara is captured, Ellaria and Tyene taken, Theon freezes and jumps overboard. Daenerys learns of the losses. Jon sails. The episode builds the alliances, betrayals, and the coming clash while the dead advance.)
2

Episode 3: The Queen's Justice
Euron Greyjoy parades captives Yara Greyjoy, Ellaria Sand, and Tyene Sand through the streets of King's Landing to the Red Keep. Crowds throw rotting fruit. Cersei is impressed with the "gift." She agrees to an alliance with Euron and calls him a true friend. Ellaria spits at Cersei's feet. The Mountain stands guard. Euron demands his reward (Cersei herself). She says after the war. She names Euron commander of her navy and Jaime commander of her armies. Jaime privately hates Euron and says his head belongs on a spike. Euron asks Jaime for tips on Cersei's sexual preferences. Jaime is furious but silent.

Later Cersei visits Ellaria and Tyene in their cell. Both are gagged and chained to opposite walls. With the Mountain and Qyburn, Cersei recalls Oberyn's fight with the Mountain and how Ellaria screamed as Oberyn died. She talks about raising Myrcella and how Ellaria murdered her. She praises Tyene's beauty and says she is Ellaria's favorite. She considers having the Mountain kill them like he killed Oberyn but decides it is too quick. She kisses Tyene on the lips with the long farewell poison (the same used on Myrcella). Qyburn confirms the poison will kill but the time varies. Cersei will leave Ellaria alive to watch her daughter's face decay to bone and dust. They will force-feed Ellaria if she tries to starve. Torches will be kept lit so she misses nothing. Ellaria struggles desperately against her chains as Cersei leaves.

That evening Jaime drinks. Cersei arrives, kisses him. He resists at first then yields. They have sex. Next morning a servant announces a visitor from Braavos. Cersei asks for fresh sheets.

Cersei meets Tycho Nestoris of the Iron Bank. He offers condolences for Tommen. He thanks her for destroying the Faith Militant, calling it superstition. Cersei knows the Bank bets on the strongest. She says Euron controls the seas as an ally for now. She paints Daenerys as a revolutionary, not a proper monarch. The Lannisters will pay their debts; Dothraki and former slaves will not. She vows to pay the Crown's debts in full within a fortnight and invites him to stay. Tycho is pleased and calls her her father's daughter.

At Winterfell, Sansa and Littlefinger learn from Maester Wolkan they have only about 4,000 bushels of wheat—not enough for winter. Sansa orders granaries built and armor lined with leather for warmth. Littlefinger urges her to fight every battle and watch every corner. A guard announces a visitor: Bran, with Meera. Sansa and Bran reunite tearfully. In the godswood Sansa wishes Jon were there. Bran needs to speak to Jon. Sansa says Bran is the rightful Lord of Winterfell as the last trueborn son. Bran refuses. He is the Three-Eyed Raven now and cannot be a lord. He proves his power by recounting details of Sansa's wedding night to Ramsay that he could not know. Sansa is shocked and walks away crying.

At the Citadel in Oldtown, Archmaester Ebrose examines Jorah Mormont. The greyscale is no longer active. Someone treated him. Jorah claims rest and climate. Ebrose releases him but will speak privately to Sam later. Jorah is returning to Daenerys because she gave him hope. He thanks Sam. Sam says it is the least he could do after Jeor Mormont's kindness. They shake hands; Jorah is moved, having thought he would never touch another person again.

Ebrose chastises Sam for the illegal, high-risk procedure but praises the success. He asks the secret. Sam says he just followed the books. Ebrose "rewards" him by ordering him to copy old manuscripts by hand so knowledge is preserved. Sam is not expelled.

Jon and Davos arrive at Dragonstone. Tyrion and Missandei greet them. Tyrion calls Jon the bastard of Winterfell; Jon calls him the dwarf of Casterly Rock. They grin. Jon notes Tyrion's scars. They hand over weapons. Missandei walks with Davos and talks of Naath. Jon and Tyrion talk of Sansa's sham marriage to Tyrion (never consummated). Sansa is smarter than she seems. Dragons Drogon and Viserion fly low; Jon and Davos dive while Tyrion and Missandei stay calm. Tyrion helps Jon up and says no one gets used to the dragons except their mother.

Varys confronts Melisandre about avoiding Jon. She parted badly because of her mistakes (Shireen). She has brought ice and fire together and will stop whispering to kings. She goes to Volantis but will return once more to die in Westeros, as will Varys.

In the throne room Missandei announces Daenerys with all titles. Davos introduces Jon simply as King in the North. Daenerys calls him a lord. There has been no King in the North since Torrhen Stark bent the knee to Aegon; oaths last forever. She demands he bend the knee. Jon refuses. She accuses him of breaking faith. He reminds her the Mad King burned his grandfather and uncle. Daenerys apologizes for her father; children should not pay for parents' crimes. She wants the old allegiance renewed. Jon agrees children should not suffer for parents but he is not bound by ancestors' oaths. He came because he needs her help and she needs his. She has dragons and Dothraki. Jon says the houses fight like children over a game while the army of the dead is the true enemy. Tyrion vouches. Jon needs alliance against the dead. Daenerys is skeptical. She recounts assassins, slavery, rape; her faith in herself hatched dragons and brought Dothraki across the sea

. Tyrion vouches. Jon needs alliance against the dead. Daenerys is skeptical. She recounts assassins, slavery, rape; her faith in herself hatched dragons and brought Dothraki across the sea. She is destined to rule the Seven Kingdoms. Jon says she will rule a graveyard if the Night King wins.

(The episode continues with the fall of Highgarden: Jaime and Randyll Tarly sack it, Olenna is captured. Jaime gives her poison as a mercy; she confesses to poisoning Joffrey and drinks it. Grey Worm takes Casterly Rock but finds it mostly empty—Jaime emptied it and used the fleet to hit the Reach. Euron destroys much of Daenerys's fleet. Theon is rescued by survivors. Jon and Daenerys's tense first meeting ends without kneeling but with the dragonglass mines opening. The story weaves Cersei's revenge, Northern reunions, Sam's quiet heroism, and the shifting war.)
3

Episode 4: The Spoils of War
At Winterfell Littlefinger meets Bran and gives him the Valyrian steel dagger the catspaw used to try to kill Bran years ago. Bran asks who it belonged to. Littlefinger says that question started the War of the Five Kings. He tries to talk of chaos. Bran quotes Littlefinger's own old words back to him: "Chaos is a ladder." Littlefinger is unnerved. Meera enters. Littlefinger leaves, calling Bran Lord Stark. Bran says he is not a lord.

Meera tells Bran she is leaving for the Neck to be with her family when the dead come. She kept her promise; he is safe now. Bran thanks her flatly. Meera is angry. Hodor, Summer, and her brother Jojen died for him. Bran says he is no longer Bran Stark. He is the Three-Eyed Raven. He remembers Bran's life but also centuries of other memories. Everything that mattered to Bran now feels distant. Meera says he died in that cave and leaves in horror.

Arya arrives at Winterfell gates. Guards do not believe she is Arya Stark (thought dead). She asks for Maester Luwin or Rodrik Cassel (both dead). She asks for Jon (just left). They say Lady Stark is in charge. Arya dodges them with assassin skill and insists she is getting in. If she is Arya they will be in trouble; if not she will not last. They let her into the courtyard and go to Sansa. When they mention Luwin and Cassel, Sansa knows it is Arya and where she will go.

Sansa finds Arya in the crypts at Ned's statue. They reunite awkwardly at first after so much pain. Arya asks if she must call her Lady Stark; Sansa says yes then laughs. They hug. Arya is glad Jon left Sansa in charge. They look at Ned's statue; it does not look like him. Arya says they still know his face. Arya asks if Sansa killed Joffrey. Sansa wishes she had. Arya says he was high on her list. They laugh about the list. Sansa asks how Arya got back; the road was hard. Sansa's was too. They hug warmly. Sansa says Bran is home. Arya's face falls when Rickon is not mentioned; she knows he is dead.

Sansa takes Arya to Bran in the godswood. Bran is detached. He is not surprised Arya is alive; he saw her at the Crossroads. Sansa explains the visions. Bran says he thought Arya was going to King's Landing because Cersei is on her list. He knows things he should not. Bran gives Arya the Valyrian steel dagger; it is wasted on a cripple. Arya takes it.

The three surviving trueborn Stark children walk back together, Arya pushing Bran's chair. Brienne and Podrick watch. Pod says Catelyn would be proud. Brienne says she did little. Pod disagrees. Brienne almost corrects "my lady" then just thanks him.

Later Brienne spars hard with Podrick. Arya interrupts and wants to spar with the woman who beat the Hound. Sansa and Littlefinger watch from above. Brienne goes easy at first. Arya uses water dancing from Syrio Forel plus Faceless Men training and finds many killing openings. Brienne stops holding back. She knocks Needle away; Arya switches to the dagger. Speed vs strength. They stalemate with blades at each other's throats. Brienne asks who taught her. Arya says "no one." They part impressed. Sansa looks concerned at Arya's deadly skill. Arya looks up at Littlefinger with distrust.

In King's Landing Cersei is happy about the gold from the Sack of Highgarden. The Lannister army is moving the gold and seizing grain. She meets Tycho Nestoris again. He is pleased she will pay the Iron Bank debts with the gold. He flatters her strategy. Cersei wants new loans to hire sellswords, specifically the Golden Company. Tycho approves once the gold arrives.

On Dragonstone Daenerys and Missandei walk to the beach to meet Jon. Missandei worries about Grey Worm (no word from Casterly Rock). Daenerys asks what happened between them; Missandei smiles "many things." Jon shows Daenerys the ancient dragonglass mine. It is vast, used by First Men long before Valyrians. Jon needs the dragonglass for the war against the dead. Daenerys is still focused on the Iron Throne but sees the caves.

(The episode's centerpiece is the Battle of the Goldroad / Loot Train Attack. Jaime and Bronn escort the gold and grain wagons from Highgarden. Daenerys arrives on Drogon with a massive Dothraki horde. Drogon burns the train and soldiers. Dothraki scream through. Jaime and Bronn fight. A scorpion bolt wounds Drogon. Jaime charges Daenerys on foot to kill her while she is down with the wounded dragon. Bronn knocks Jaime into the water with a tackle just as Drogon breathes fire. They survive. Tyrion watches the slaughter from afar, horrified at the destruction. Arya, Sansa, Bran reunite fully. The spoils of war shift: Lannisters have gold but lose the train and many men; Daenerys shows her power but loses the chance for a clean victory without fire and blood.)
4

Episode 5: Eastwatch
After the Battle of the Goldroad, Bronn pulls Jaime from the Blackwater Rush. Bronn says he saved Jaime only because no one kills Jaime until Bronn gets his castle and reward. Jaime is shocked by Drogon's power. If Daenerys uses all three dragons they are doomed. Bronn jokes it is safer to jump back in the river than face Cersei's anger.

On the Goldroad Daenerys and Tyrion face the Lannister and Tarly prisoners. Drogon perches behind her. She offers them a choice: bend the knee and help break the wheel of power that crushes everyone for people like Cersei, or die. Few kneel at first. Drogon roars; most kneel. Randyll Tarly and his son Dickon refuse. Randyll already has a queen. Tyrion notes Randyll's flexible loyalties (he only recently joined Cersei after she destroyed the Tyrells). Randyll calls Tyrion a kinslayer and Daenerys a foreigner with savages. Tyrion suggests the Wall. Randyll says she is not his queen so she cannot send him. Dickon stands with his father. Tyrion begs Dickon to live as the future of House Tarly. Randyll silently nods for his son to kneel and live. Dickon refuses. Daenerys will not put traitors in chains; it would encourage others. She has Drogon burn Randyll and Dickon alive. They hold hands as they die in seconds. The rest kneel in terror. Tyrion looks uneasy.

At Winterfell Bran wargs into ravens and flies beyond the Wall. He sees the army of the dead, White Walkers, and the Night King heading for Eastwatch-by-the-Sea. The Night King sees the ravens; Bran breaks the connection. He tells Maester Wolkan to send ravens at once warning everyone.

In the council chamber Arya watches Sansa preside. Lords Glover and Royce imply they chose the wrong ruler and that Sansa should take power while Jon is away. Sansa insists Jon is their king doing what is right and she is only regent. Afterward Sansa vents to Arya about the lords. Arya says Sansa should shut them down hard, even kill them for insulting Jon. Sansa disagrees. Arya notes Sansa uses their parents' chambers and still acts superior—maybe she wants the North for herself. Sansa is hurt and disturbed by Arya's killer instincts. She has work to do.

Arya stalks Littlefinger. She sees him talk to a servant, then to Maester Wolkan about "the only copy." She sneaks into his room, finds under the mattress the old letter Sansa wrote to Robb urging him to bend the knee to Joffrey (written under Cersei's duress to try to save Ned). Arya is horrified, not knowing the full context. She takes it. Littlefinger watches from hiding and grins.

At the Citadel the maesters read Bran's warning about the dead and dismiss it as myth or Daenerys disinformation. Sam defends Bran. Archmaester Ebrose agrees to investigate further but is skeptical. After Sam leaves they note his father and brother were just burned alive; Ebrose has not told him yet.

That night Gilly reads an old High Septon diary. It records an annulment for "Prince Ragger" (Rhaegar) so he could marry another in Dorne. This would make any child of that marriage trueborn. Neither Gilly nor Sam grasps the full meaning for Jon. Sam is miserable copying bodily functions of old septons. He quits, grabs books, and leaves the Citadel with Gilly and little Sam that night. He is tired of reading about better men's achievements.

On Dragonstone Jon walks the grounds. Daenerys arrives on Drogon. The dragon roars at Jon then calms and lets Jon stroke his snout (sensing Targaryen blood?). Daenerys is surprised. She calls the dragons her children. She has fewer enemies now. They talk of the Battle of the Bastards and Jon taking a knife for his people. Jon deflects. Jorah Mormont returns, healed. Daenerys introduces him to Jon (who served under Jeor). Jorah reaffirms loyalty; she hugs him.

Tyrion and Varys discuss the Tarly executions. Varys worries Daenerys has a ruthless streak like her father that Tyrion must curb. They have Bran's message about the dead.

(The episode builds to the decision for a wight hunt. Jon proposes capturing a wight beyond the Wall to prove the threat to Cersei so she will join the fight. Daenerys is reluctant but agrees to let him go with a small party. Gendry arrives from King's Landing with a message and joins. The group forms: Jon, Jorah, Gendry, Tormund, Beric, Thoros, Sandor, and others. They head to Eastwatch. Theon returns to Daenerys seeking ships to save Yara; she allows it after he admits his failures. Tensions at Winterfell between the sisters grow with Littlefinger's schemes. The dead close in on Eastwatch.)
5

Episode 6: Beyond the Wall
At Winterfell Arya talks to Sansa about practicing with Bran's bow until she hit the bullseye while Ned watched and clapped. She says Ned knew the rules were wrong but she was right. She confronts Sansa with the letter Sansa wrote to Robb. Sansa explains Cersei forced her. Arya says she was not tortured and she saw Sansa at Ned's execution (Sansa did nothing either). Arya accuses betrayal. Sansa says they are only home because of her efforts; Arya chased her own list. The Knights of the Vale (Littlefinger) saved Jon. Arya would not have survived what Sansa did with Joffrey and Ramsay. Sansa asks where the letter came from. Arya realizes Sansa fears the Northern lords (especially Lyanna Mormont) finding it. Arya prefers anger to fear.

Sansa asks Littlefinger about the letter (not knowing he planted it). She commands 20,000 men loyal to Jon, not her. Littlefinger says the men will trust her ability to rule. Sansa fears the letter will turn them. He suggests talking to Brienne, who swore to protect both daughters. Sansa agrees.

Maester Wolkan brings a letter from Cersei. Sansa decides to send Brienne as envoy to the parley (Brienne can reason with Jaime). Brienne warns it is dangerous to leave Sansa alone with Littlefinger. Sansa insists her men are loyal. Brienne offers to leave Podrick; Sansa declines.

Later Sansa enters Arya's room and finds a case of faces, including Walder Frey's. Arya catches her. Arya forces the "game of faces" / lying game. She asks if Sansa thinks Jon is the rightful king. Arya explains the faces from the Faceless Men. They always wanted to be other people: Sansa a queen, Arya a knight. Neither got it. The faces let her become someone else. She toys with taking Sansa's face and becoming Lady of Winterfell, approaching with the dagger. Then she relents and leaves Sansa shaken with the dagger.

At Dragonstone Daenerys and Tyrion talk. She likes that he is not a hero who does stupid dangerous things. She lists past loves who were heroes: Drogo, Jorah, Daario, Jon. Tyrion notes they all fell in love with her. She dismisses that Jon is in love. She accidentally insults Tyrion's height then apologizes. They discuss the coming meeting with Cersei. Tyrion knows she cannot be trusted but Daenerys has armies and dragons as backup. Daenerys wonders if they should plan deceit too. Tyrion is against ruling only by fear (like Cersei, Tywin, Joffrey). She must break the wheel, not become the next tyrant. He criticizes the Tarly executions as too hasty. She blames his caution for losses of Highgarden, Ellaria, Yara. She will not discuss succession (she believes she cannot have children) until she has the crown.

Beyond the Wall the ranging party (Jon, Jorah, Gendry, Tormund, Beric, Thoros, Sandor, and wildlings/Night's Watch) trudges through snow. Gendry complains of cold; Tormund talks wildling life. Tormund tells Jon the mission is foolhardy; Northern pride costs lives (like Mance). Jon talks of hard talks with Daenerys. Gendry confronts the Brotherhood about selling him to Melisandre. Sandor says be grateful he is alive; Beric has died six times and does not complain. They drink.

Jon and Jorah talk of their honorable fathers who did not deserve their deaths (Jeor by mutineers, Ned beheaded). Jon tries to give Longclaw back. Jorah says he is not worthy after shaming his house. His father gave it to Jon; keep it for himself and his children.

Sandor and Tormund banter about sex. Tormund asks about Sandor's burns; Sandor is offended. Tormund talks of his crush on Brienne and "monstrous" babies. Beric and Jon talk of resurrection by the Lord of Light and fighting death as the enemy. Jon recalls the Night's Watch oath as the shield that guards the realms of men. Sandor sees the arrowhead mountain from his vision and leads them that way.

In a snowstorm they are attacked by a massive undead snow bear (blue eyes, rotting). It kills three men. Beric sets it on fire with his sword but it keeps coming. Thoros is mauled saving Sandor (who freezes at the flames). Jorah kills it with dragonglass. Beric cauterizes Thoros's wounds with his flaming sword. They follow the tracks.

They find a White Walker leading a small group of wights. They ambush. Jon kills the White Walker with Longclaw; the wights it raised collapse except one. They capture the last wight, chain it, and start back. But a massive army of the dead has been signaled and pursues. The party runs, fighting rearguard actions. They reach a frozen lake. The wights stop at the thin ice. The group is trapped on a rock island in the middle as night falls and the dead surround them on all sides. Thoros dies of his wounds; Beric cannot revive him. Gendry is sent running back to Eastwatch to raven Daenerys for help. They wait in the cold, burning the last wood, fighting off probes when the ice thickens.

Daenerys, against Tyrion's counsel, flies north with all three dragons to rescue them. The dragons burn swathes of wights. The party climbs onto the dragons. The Night King appears, takes an ice spear, and hurls it with perfect aim. It pierces Viserion through the neck. Viserion crashes, thrashing, and dies. Daenerys is devastated. Another spear nearly hits Drogon. They escape, but Jon is separated, pulled down fighting. Benjen Stark (Coldhands) suddenly appears on horseback, rescues Jon, and sacrifices himself holding off the dead so Jon can reach the Wall.

At Eastwatch Tormund and others pull Jon inside. Daenerys waits. Jon, half-frozen, finally bends the knee and calls her his queen. He swears loyalty. She accepts, emotional over Viserion. They sail south with the captured wight.

(The Winterfell sister confrontation escalates with the faces and dagger. Littlefinger's schemes continue. The wight hunt is desperate, costly, and succeeds only at the price of a dragon. The Night King now has an undead dragon.)

Episode 7: The Dragon and the Wolf
Outside King's Landing the Unsullied under Grey Worm form ranks. Dothraki hordes ride past. On the walls Jaime and Bronn watch. Bronn is unnerved by soldiers without genitals who fight without the usual motivations. The two armies (former enemies) stand together for the parley.

Tyrion, Varys, Missandei, Jon, Davos, and Sandor (with the caged wight) sail past Euron's fleet into the harbor. Cersei is told Daenerys's party has arrived (no Daenerys yet). She orders the Mountain: if anything goes wrong, kill Daenerys, then Tyrion, then Jon, then the rest.

They go to the Dragonpit for the summit. Tyrion greets Bronn (awkwardly friendly). Podrick is there with Brienne. Brienne and Sandor talk: they only fought over Arya; now Arya needs no protection—worry about whoever stands in her way. Sandor is amused.

The factions gather: Cersei, Jaime, Qyburn, Euron for the crown; Jon, Davos, Brienne for the North; Daenerys's people. Cersei asks where her rival is. Daenerys makes a dramatic entrance on Drogon, Rhaegal overhead. Sandor comes face to helmet with the Mountain and promises to finish him later. He goes to get the wight.

Euron postures, threatens Yara unless Theon yields, mocks Tyrion's size. Tyrion and Theon fire back. Euron says dwarfs are killed at birth on the Iron Islands. Jaime orders him to sit; Cersei repeats it. Euron sits.

Tyrion and Jon explain the army of the dead. A million people in King's Landing will become a million more wights. Cersei is flippant; it might improve them. Jon is angered. She thinks it is a trick. Sandor kicks over the crate. The wight bursts out, charges Cersei. Sandor chains it, cuts it in half. The torso keeps crawling and screeching. He cuts off a hand. Qyburn examines. Jon burns the hand with a torch (fire kills them) then stabs the torso with dragonglass, killing it. He says this fate awaits everyone if they lose. All other wars are nothing beside the Great War. Daenerys says she did not believe until she saw. Jaime asks how many; at least 100,000. Euron asks if they swim. Jon says no. Euron announces he is taking his fleet back to the Iron Islands. Nothing has ever terrified him like this. He tells Daenerys to find him when only they two are left.

Cersei admits fear but says running is foolish. She offers: her armies will not hinder the fight against the dead, but she will not deal with Daenerys. She wants Jon (as Ned's son and King in the North) to stay out of any future Cersei-Daenerys war. Jon says he cannot serve two queens. He has already bent the knee to Daenerys. The Lannisters are furious. Cersei storms out. No truce if it is just her versus Daenerys. She will let them fight the dead then deal with the winner. Brienne begs Jaime to stay and help; this is bigger than houses and thrones. Jaime walks away.

Daenerys and Tyrion criticize Jon for declaring publicly. Tyrion says learning to lie a little helps. Daenerys says without alliance Viserion died for nothing. Jon says if no one speaks truth, words are worthless. Lies will not win the war. Tyrion goes alone to try to convince Cersei.

In the Red Keep Tyrion meets Jaime, who believes the threat but could not convince Cersei. Tyrion enters. They trade barbs. Cersei blames Tyrion for Tywin's death and the cascade that killed her children and the Lannister future. Tyrion says Tywin deserved it for the abuse and false trial. He loved Myrcella and Tommen. He calls her bluff: if she truly blames him, have the Mountain kill him now. She does not. They drink. She accuses him of plotting with Jon and Daenerys to destroy the Lannisters. He did not know Jon had sworn. Without him Daenerys would have burned the Red Keep. He serves her to curb her excesses; Cersei indulges hers. She talks of protecting those she loves and fleeing like Euron. Tyrion realizes she is pregnant.

Back at the Dragonpit Daenerys and Jon talk of dragons caged by her ancestors and how the family diminished as dragon power faded. Jon questions her belief she cannot have children (only Mirri Maz Duur said so). The Lannisters return. Cersei agrees to the truce: the Lannister army will march north to fight the dead alongside them.

(Later private scenes reveal Cersei's lie to Jaime. She will not send her army north. She will let the others weaken themselves against the dead, then strike. Jaime is disgusted by the betrayal and the pregnancy news used as leverage. He leaves her and rides north alone.

At Winterfell Littlefinger's schemes peak. He tries to turn Sansa and Arya fully against each other. Bran reveals he knows everything. In the great hall Sansa puts Littlefinger on trial with Arya and Bran. The charges: murder of Lysa Arryn, betrayal of Ned, starting the war, playing everyone. Littlefinger begs, crawls, claims love for Catelyn and Sansa. Arya holds the Valyrian steel dagger to his throat. Sansa sentences him. Arya cuts his throat. Littlefinger dies. The Stark siblings stand united.

Sam arrives at Winterfell with Gilly and the baby. He tells Bran and the others what he learned in the Citadel scrolls and the diary: Rhaegar had his marriage to Elia annulled and secretly married Lyanna Stark. Jon is their trueborn son, Aegon Targaryen, rightful heir. Bran confirms with his visions of the Tower of Joy: Lyanna's dying words to Ned, "His name is Aegon Targaryen. Promise me, Ned." Jon is not a bastard.

Theon raids to free Yara from Euron's ship and succeeds.
